exp_design: Each experiment had 13 treatments arrangement with 3 replications in a randomized complete block design. Each plot size was 6 × 3 m.
time_raw: Experiments were conducted during the rainy seasons of two consecutive years (2003 and 2004). Baby corn (Zea mays L. cv. VL-16), soybean (Glycine max cv. Alankar), green gram (Phaseolus aureus Roxb. cv. B-105), black gram (Vigna mungo Roxb. cv. T-9), and groundnut (Arachis hypogea cv. GG-2) were sown on June 18, 2003 and June 24, 2004. Baby corn was harvested on September 8, 2003 and September 11, 2004, whereas Green gram and black gram were harvested on September 15, 2003 and September 29, 2004. Soybean and groundnut were harvested on October 4, 2003 and October 15, 2004.
subpractice_description_raw: Baby corn sown at 60 cm spacing as monocrop
tillage_subpractice_raw: power tiller ploughing followed by harrowing
intercrop_subpractice_raw: monocultre
fert_subpractice_raw: The fertilizer schedule was 150:100:100 kg N, P2O5 and K2O ha−1 for monocropped and intercropped baby corn and 40:60:60 (N, P2O5, K2O) for monocropped legumes. Half of the N was applied through vermicompost (1.5–0.65–1.2) in baby corn as basal application. Proportionate fertilizers were also applied to intercropped legumes along the rows. One-fourth of nitrogen in the form of urea (46–0–0) and the whole amount of P2O5 and K2O in the form of single super phosphate (0–16–0) and muriate of potash (0–0–60) respectively were applied as basal and remaining one-fourth nitrogen was top dressed at 30 days after sowing (DAS). The total amount of N, P2O5, and K2O in the form of urea, SSP, and MOP was applied as basal in legumes.
weed_method_raw: Weeding operations were accomplished at 20 and 40 days after sowing.
out_exp_design: Each plot size was 6 × 3 m.

site_id: Indian Statistical Institute, Giridih

site_id01: Indian Statistical Institute, Giridih
exp_design: Each experiment had 13 treatments arrangement with 3 replications in a randomized complete block design. Each plot size was 6 × 3 m.
time_raw: Experiments were conducted during the rainy seasons of two consecutive years (2003 and 2004). Baby corn (Zea mays L. cv. VL-16), soybean (Glycine max cv. Alankar), green gram (Phaseolus aureus Roxb. cv. B-105), black gram (Vigna mungo Roxb. cv. T-9), and groundnut (Arachis hypogea cv. GG-2) were sown on June 18, 2003 and June 24, 2004. Baby corn was harvested on September 8, 2003 and September 11, 2004, whereas Green gram and black gram were harvested on September 15, 2003 and September 29, 2004. Soybean and groundnut were harvested on October 4, 2003 and October 15, 2004.
subpractice_description_raw: One row of soybean sown at 30 cm spacing in between of two rows of baby corn
tillage_subpractice_raw: power tiller ploughing followed by harrowing
intercrop_subpractice_raw: intercropping 2:1 row additive
intercrop_subpractice: Intercrop (N fixing and Non N fixing)
fert_subpractice_raw: The fertilizer schedule was 150:100:100 kg N, P2O5 and K2O ha−1 for monocropped and intercropped baby corn and 40:60:60 (N, P2O5, K2O) for monocropped legumes. Half of the N was applied through vermicompost (1.5–0.65–1.2) in baby corn as basal application. Proportionate fertilizers were also applied to intercropped legumes along the rows. One-fourth of nitrogen in the form of urea (46–0–0) and the whole amount of P2O5 and K2O in the form of single super phosphate (0–16–0) and muriate of potash (0–0–60) respectively were applied as basal and remaining one-fourth nitrogen was top dressed at 30 days after sowing (DAS). The total amount of N, P2O5, and K2O in the form of urea, SSP, and MOP was applied as basal in legumes.
weed_method_raw: Weeding operations were accomplished at 20 and 40 days after sowing.
out_exp_design: Each plot size was 6 × 3 m.

out_subindicator_description_raw: Total tomato yield obtained under the conditions of this study
extraction_obs: Experiment time calculated on days after treatment, which is 127 + 5 series of 8 days for tomato pickings after day 127, giving 167 days.
